title: Test-run registration POST can stall past the launcher's 8 s budget (post_headers), aborting a focused run before any test starts
outcome: Observed 2026-10-19, filed by Termal::Fable2. (1) Sol-c593's focused run test-e0f5f5da-7981-4efc-9b80-50e2df7c33a9 at about 18:59Z aborted before any Cargo or tests: registration POST send aborted at post_headers after 8004.4 ms against the 8000 ms budget, HTTP unavailable (operation 442436b0-09c6-44be-b9a1-b834a3197785, digest b8294f04…; run directory preserved in its Git-admin review-runs). (2) Coder's M5 full-gate registration at 18:37Z took 5948.8 ms of the 8000 ms budget, with post_headers 0–3750 ms and get_headers 3751–5947 ms. At the time, the central host (instance c25c5f07, just restarted) was running a full gate in vitest, an Engram warm, a TermAl warm and a remote Mac session. /api/health answered in about 40 ms at 18:59Z, and /api/test-runs in 361 ms. Hypotheses to discriminate: host request handling blocked on the shared state lock or a blocking persist during registration; a slow /api/test-runs-style projection on the registration path; or machine load. Do NOT fix by raising the budget. Find where the POST stalls (the host-side span) and remove the blocking cause.
acceptance: The host-side cause of multi-second registration POST latency is identified with evidence (timed spans or a discriminating reproduction under concurrent load), and fixed so registration completes well within budget under that load; a test or measured reproduction shows it, with no budget increase.
The full five-stage gate passes on the exact input with an independent Codex plus Claude review pair and no outstanding in-scope Medium-or-higher finding.
